questions.question: Who holds the position of President of the International Criminal Court (as of April 2025)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Judge Tomoko Akane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Judge Tomoko Akane** is a distinguished **Japanese legal expert** who has held various judicial and prosecutorial positions throughout her career.
 
• She was elected as the President of the International Criminal Court (ICC) for the term starting in 2024 and continuing through 2027, according to the latest information.
 
• Judge Akane has been a member of the ICC since 2018, contributing to international justice and global accountability systems.
 
• Her appointment as President reflects her extensive expertise in criminal law, international law, and judicial administration.
 
• The ICC, based in The Hague, Netherlands, is an independent judicial institution responsible for prosecuting individuals for crimes such as genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Criminal Court (ICC):**

 
 
• The ICC was established by the Rome Statute, which came into force on** 1 July 2002**.
 
• It is the first permanent international court set up to prosecute individuals for the most serious offenses of concern to the international community.
 
• The ICC operates independently from the United Nations, although they cooperate on various issues.
 
 
 
• **Rome Statute:**
 
 
• This treaty serves as the foundation of the ICC and outlines its jurisdiction, structure, and functioning.
 
• As of 2023, 123 countries are State Parties to the Rome Statute.
 
• Key crimes under the ICC’s jurisdiction include genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, and the crime of aggression.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Structure of the ICC:**
 
 
• The ICC is composed of 18 judges, elected by the Assembly of States Parties for nine-year terms.
 
• Judges are divided among Pre-Trial, Trial, and Appeals Chambers to ensure fair and efficient proceedings.
 
• The President, along with two Vice-Presidents, is elected from among the judges for a three-year term.
 
 
 
• **Role of the ICC President:**
 
 
• The President oversees the overall administration of the ICC, ensuring its effective functioning.
 
• They represent the Court in external relations and play a crucial role in managing its judicial and administrative activities.

questions.question: Who among the following was awarded with the MS Swaminathan Environment Protection Award 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anant Darshan Shankar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The** MS Swaminathan Environment Protection Award** is instituted to recognize individuals or organizations for their contributions towards **environmental protection and sustainable development.**
 
• In 2024, **Anant Darshan Shankar**, a pioneer in the field of integrative health sciences and traditional knowledge systems, was honored with this award.
 
• Anant Darshan Shankar is the **Founder of the Foundation for Revitalisation of Local Health Traditions (FRLHT)**, which focuses on conservation and sustainable use of medicinal plants and local health traditions.
 
• The award highlights his significant efforts in **promoting biodiversity conservation and sustainable practices** for the protection of the environment.
 
• The recognition also underscores the role of traditional knowledge in addressing contemporary environmental challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MS Swaminathan:**

 
 
• Known as the **"Father of the Green Revolution in India,"** MS Swaminathan played a crucial role in introducing high-yielding crop varieties to Indian agriculture.
 
• He emphasized the importance of sustainable and environment-friendly agricultural practices.
 
 
 
• **Integrative Health Sciences:**
 
 
• It is an approach that combines modern medical practices with traditional knowledge systems to promote holistic well-being.
 
• Anant Darshan Shankar has been a strong advocate for this approach, particularly in the context of biodiversity conservation.
 
 
 
• **Foundation for Revitalisation of Local Health Traditions (FRLHT):**
 
 
• A Bengaluru-based organization founded by Anant Darshan Shankar in 1993.
 
• It works to preserve traditional health practices and medicinal plant species through research and community engagement.
 
 
 
• **Medicinal Plant Conservation:**
 
 
• Medicinal plants are critical for both traditional medicine systems and modern pharmaceuticals.
 
• Conservation efforts focus on sustainable harvesting, cultivation, and protection of biodiversity.

questions.question: As per the Union Budget 2025-26, what is the total number of Gram Panchayats in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.68 lakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India has a total of **2.68 lakh Gram Panchayats** as per the Union Budget 2025-26.
 
• Gram Panchayats are the **foundation of the local self-governance system** under the Panchayati Raj framework.
 
• The Union Budget 2025-26 allocated resources for **strengthening rural infrastructure** and empowering Gram Panchayats.
 
• The **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act** established the Panchayati Raj system, giving Gram Panchayats a constitutional status.
 
• Gram Panchayats play a crucial role in **implementing government schemes**, ensuring rural development, and promoting community participation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gram Panchayat:**

 
 
• Gram Panchayat is the lowest administrative unit in India’s rural governance system.
 
• It operates under the Panchayati Raj system, which is a decentralized form of governance.
 
• Each Gram Panchayat typically covers one or more villages.
 
 
 
• **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act:**
 
 
• Passed in 1992, it provided constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs).
 
• The Act mandates regular elections, reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women, and a three-tier governance system.
 
• It emphasizes grassroots democracy and decentralized planning.
 
 
 
• **Role of Gram Panchayats:**
 
 
• Gram Panchayats are responsible for implementing government schemes like MGNREGA, Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, and PMAY.
 
• They handle local administration, sanitation, water supply, and infrastructure development.
 
• They act as a platform for community participation in decision-making processes.
 
 
 
• **Panchayati Raj System:**
 
 
• The Panchayati Raj System is a three-tier structure consisting of Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, and Zilla Parishad.
 
• It is aimed at decentralizing power and promoting democratic governance at the local level.
 
• It plays a vital role in India’s rural development and socio-economic empowerment.

questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India has its offices in how many locations in India, as of April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**33 locations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As of April 2025, **the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has offices in 33 locations across India**.
 
• These offices include regional offices, sub-offices, and branches located in major cities to oversee monetary policy implementation and banking regulation.
 
• The RBI's network is designed to ensure effective supervision of financial institutions and promote economic stability across different regions.
 
• Key locations include Mumbai (headquarters),** Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad**, among others.
 
• The RBI also has specialized offices for foreign exchange management, banking supervision, and financial inclusion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**

 
 
• The RBI is India's central bank, established on April 1, 1935, under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• Its primary functions include regulating the issuance of currency, controlling inflation, supervising banks, and managing foreign exchange.
 
• The RBI plays a key role in implementing monetary policy to ensure economic stability and growth.
 
 
 
• **Regional Offices:**
 
 
• Regional offices are located in major cities to facilitate communication between the central bank and local banks.
 
• They also oversee the implementation of RBI policies in their respective regions.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy:**
 
 
• The RBI formulates and implements monetary policy to control inflation, stabilize the currency, and promote economic growth.
 
• Key tools of monetary policy include the repo rate, reverse repo rate, and cash reserve ratio (CRR).
 
 
 
• **Banking Regulation:**
 
 
• The RBI supervises and regulates India's banking sector to ensure stability and trustworthiness in the financial system.
 
• It also manages the licensing of banks and monitors their compliance with financial regulations.
 
 
 
• **Financial Inclusion:**
 
 
• The RBI actively promotes financial inclusion to ensure access to banking services for underserved and rural areas.
 
• Initiatives include promoting digital payments, opening no-frills accounts, and improving banking infrastructure in remote regions.

questions.question: In February 2025, which day was celebrated to honour the Nightingale of India, Sarojini Naidu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Women's Day**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **National Women's Day **in India is celebrated on **February 13th** every year to honor **Sarojini Naidu**, popularly known as the **Nightingale of India**.
 
• Sarojini Naidu was born on **February 13, 1879**, and the day is marked to commemorate her contributions to Indian society.
 
• She was a prominent freedom fighter, poet, and the first woman to become the president of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Sarojini Naidu also served as the **first woman governor of an Indian state** (Uttar Pradesh) after independence.
 
• Her literary works and political achievements have left an indelible mark on Indian history and women's empowerment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarojini Naidu's Legacy:**

 
 
• She is remembered for her collection of poems such as **"The Golden Threshold"**, "**The Bird of Time**," and "**The Broken Wing**."
 
• Her poetry often highlighted themes of patriotism, nature, and love.
 
• Sarojini Naidu played a critical role in the Civil Disobedience Movement and the Quit India Movement.
 
 
 
• **Role in Indian Freedom Struggle:**
 
 
• She worked closely with Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and other leaders during the Indian independence movement.
 
• She was a staunch advocate of women's rights and education.
 
 
 
• **Recognition and Impact:**
 
 
• Sarojini Naidu's birthday is celebrated as National Women's Day to inspire women to achieve greatness.
 
• Her life symbolizes the blend of art and activism, making her a role model for generations.

questions.question: What was the percentage distribution of persons in the age group 15-59 years (both rural and urban) who did NOT receive vocational/technical training, as per PLFS 2021 22?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.805**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2021-22, approximately **80.5% of individuals** in the age group 15-59 years in both rural and urban areas did NOT receive vocational/technical training.
 
• The PLFS is conducted annually by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
 
• The survey provides crucial insights into employment, unemployment, and labor force participation in India.
 
• Vocational training refers to **skill-based training** designed to prepare individuals for specific jobs or professions.
 
• The findings highlight the significant gap in vocational skill development among the working-age population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS):**

 
 
• Launched in **April 2017** by NSO.
 
• Aims to provide annual estimates of employment and unemployment indicators.
 
• Covers rural and urban areas across India.
 
• The survey includes **parameters like vocational training, education, and gender-based workforce participation.**
 
 
 
• **Vocational Training:**
 
 
• Training designed to equip individuals with **specific skills for particular jobs.**
 
• Examples include training in IT, plumbing, electrical work, healthcare, and other technical fields.
 
• Plays a critical role in enhancing employability and productivity.
 
 
 
• **Skill Development Initiatives in India:**
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY):** A flagship scheme to train and certify youth in various skills.
 
• India has set up **National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC)** to promote skill development programs.
 
• Efforts include partnerships with industries and global organizations for better implementation.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Vocational Training:**
 
 
• Lack of awareness and accessibility to training facilities in rural areas.
 
• Mismatch between skills imparted and industry requirements.
 
• Low enrollment rates due to socio-economic barriers.

questions.question: In the 2024 Global Innovation Index, which organisation ranked India 39th among 133 global economies, highlighting its leadership in the Central and Southern Asian region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**World Intellectual Property Organization**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)** is a specialized agency of the **United Nations** responsible for** promoting intellectual property rights worldwide**.
 
• **India **ranked **39th among 133 global economies** in the **2024 Global Innovation Index** (GII), showcasing its leadership in the **Central and Southern Asian region**.
 
• The Global Innovation Index is published annually by **WIPO **in collaboration with other institutions such as **Cornell University and INSEAD**.
 
• The GII evaluates economies based on **innovation capabilities and results** using indicators like research, infrastructure, and business sophistication.
 
• India’s consistent improvement in ranking reflects its focus on **enhancing education, research, and technology-driven sectors**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO):**

 
 
• Founded in 1967, WIPO is headquartered in **Geneva, Switzerland**.
 
• Its mission is to lead the development of a balanced and effective international intellectual property (IP) system.
 
• WIPO provides services for **international IP protection** such as patents, trademarks, and copyrights.
 
• The organization currently has **193 member states**.
 
 
 
• **Global Innovation Index (GII):**
 
 
• The GII ranks countries based on their innovation performance using over 80 indicators.
 
• It is recognized globally as a benchmark for assessing innovation policies and outcomes.
 
• The index covers areas like **human capital, research, market sophistication, and knowledge creation**.
 
• India has been consistently improving its rank, demonstrating advancements in **digital infrastructure, startup ecosystem, and R&D activities**.
 
 
 
• **India’s Innovation Ecosystem:**
 
 
• India has achieved global recognition for its **startup-friendly policies and technological advancements**.
 
• Initiatives like **Digital India, Make in India, and Atal Innovation Mission** have contributed to enhancing the innovation landscape.
 
• India is a hub for sectors like , ITpharmaceuticals, and space technology, driving international collaborations.
 
• Emphasis on higher education and research institutions has strengthened India’s position on the GII.

questions.question: Which country assumed the presidency of BRICS in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brazil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Brazil **assumed the **presidency of BRICS **in **January 2025**, continuing the annual rotation of leadership among member countries.
 
• BRICS is an acronym for five major emerging economies:** Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa**.
 
• The presidency of BRICS rotates annually in alphabetical order among its members.
 
• As the BRICS president, Brazil will oversee hosting summits, coordinating initiatives, and aligning efforts for economic cooperation among member countries in 2025.
 
• The BRICS presidency allows member countries to shape agendas focusing on global economic challenges and sustainable development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BRICS Overview**

 
 
• BRICS was established in **2006**, **initially consisting of Brazil, Russia, India, and China, with South Africa joining in 2010**.
 
• The organization focuses on fostering cooperation in areas such as trade, finance, infrastructure, and sustainable development.
 
• The BRICS nations collectively represent approximately** 40% of the global population and over 20% of the world’s GDP**.
 
 
 
• **BRICS Presidency**
 
 
• The presidency rotates alphabetically among member countries every year.
 
• Responsibilities include hosting the annual BRICS summit, coordinating agendas, and spearheading collaborative efforts.
 
• South Africa held the presidency in 2023, followed by Russia in 2024, and Brazil in 2025.
 
 
 
• **Key Initiatives by BRICS**
 
 
• **New Development Bank** (NDB): Established in **2014 **to fund infrastructure and sustainable development projects.
 
• Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA): A framework to provide financial support during global economic crises.
 
• BRICS Business Council: Promotes business collaboration among member nations.
 
 
 
• **Impact of BRICS**
 
 
• BRICS plays a significant role in advocating for reforms in global financial institutions like the IMF and World Bank.
 
• It emphasizes addressing global challenges such as **climate change, poverty, and inequality**.
 
• The group seeks to create a multipolar world order, reducing reliance on Western-dominated institutions.

questions.question: In May 2025, Jenu Kuruba families reoccupied their ancestral land in which of the following tiger reserves of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagarahole Tiger Reserve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Jenu Kuruba** is a tribal community primarily residing in the forests of Karnataka, and their ancestral land falls within the **Nagarahole Tiger Reserve**.
 
• **Nagarahole Tiger Reserve** is located in the state of **Karnataka**, India, and is part of the **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve**.
 
• The reoccupation of ancestral land by Jenu Kuruba families in May 2025 highlights the ongoing struggle for tribal rights and access to traditional forest lands.
 
• Nagarahole Tiger Reserve is known for its rich biodiversity, including tigers, elephants, and other wildlife, making it a critical conservation area.
 
• The reserve is also a **UNESCO World Heritage Site **as part of the Western Ghats, recognized for its ecological importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jenu Kuruba Tribe:**

 
 
• The Jenu Kuruba tribe derives its name from "Jenu," meaning honey, which they traditionally collected from forests.
 
• They are one of the prominent Scheduled Tribes in Karnataka, known for their deep connection to forest ecosystems.
 
• The tribe practices sustainable forest-based livelihoods, including honey collection and small-scale agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Nagarahole Tiger Reserve:**
 
 
• It spans two districts: Mysore and Kodagu in Karnataka.
 
• The reserve covers an area of approximately 640 square kilometers and is part of the larger Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.
 
• It features tropical moist and dry deciduous forests, providing habitat for a wide range of species.
 
 
 
• **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve:**
 
 
• It is the first biosphere reserve established in India in 1986.
 
• Spread across Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka, the reserve supports diverse flora and fauna.
 
• The area is critical for conserving endemic species and maintaining ecological balance.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India:**
 
 
• The Western Ghats, which include the Nagarahole Tiger Reserve, are recognized by UNESCO for their unique biodiversity.
 
• India has 40 UNESCO World Heritage Sites as of 2023, including cultural and natural landmarks.
 
• World Heritage status ensures global recognition and support for preservation efforts.

questions.question: In March 2025, India successfully tested a high-energy laser-directed weapon system, becoming the fourth nation globally to achieve this feat. Which countries had previously developed such systems?

options.text: The US, The UK and France

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The US, Russia and China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **India** successfully tested a **high-energy laser-directed weapon system** in **March 2025**, becoming the fourth nation globally to achieve this milestone.
 
• The countries that had previously developed high-energy laser-directed weapon systems are **The US, Russia, and China**.
 
• The US has been a pioneer in laser weapons development, with systems like the Laser Weapon System (LaWS) deployed by the Navy.
 
• Russia has made advancements in laser-directed weapons, such as the Peresvet laser system designed for air defense and anti-satellite purposes.
 
• China has also developed laser weapons for military applications, including systems aimed at disabling drones and satellites.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High-Energy Laser Weapons:**

 
 
• These weapons use focused laser beams to target and disable enemy assets such as drones, missiles, and vehicles.
 
• They rely on **directed energy technology**, offering precision targeting with minimal collateral damage.
 
• Laser weapons are cost-effective as they eliminate the need for conventional ammunition.
 
 
 
• **India's Defense Technological Advancements:**
 
 
• India has invested significantly in indigenous defense technologies under initiatives like **Make in India**.
 
• The laser-directed weapon system represents a major leap in India's defense capabilities, reinforcing its status as a global military power.
 
 
 
• **Global Context of Directed Energy Weapons:**
 
 
• Directed energy weapons are gaining prominence due to their ability to counter emerging threats like drones and hypersonic missiles.
 
• Countries like **The US, Russia, and China** are actively integrating these systems into their defense architectures.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Laser Weapon Development:**
 
 
• Technological challenges include energy storage, heat dissipation, and operational effectiveness under diverse conditions.
 
• Operational deployment requires significant advancements in power generation and mobility.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the 'Trinetra' project, developed by IIT Tirupati?

• 'Trinetra' aligns with the growing need for awareness about cyber risks due to increasing digital dependence in daily activities.

• Cybersecurity awareness involves understanding the risks associated with online activities and adopting safe practices to protect personal and organizational data.

• India has witnessed a significant increase in cyber incidents, prompting the need for initiatives to enhance cybersecurity education and awareness.

questions.question: What significant achievement did Mohun Bagan Super Giant accomplish by winning the ISL 2024-25 title?

options.text: They won the title with a 100% win rate at home.
They became the second team to win both the ISL League Shield and ISL Cup in the same season.
They won the title without losing a single match.
They became the first team to win the ISL title twice.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They became the second team to win both the ISL League Shield and ISL Cup in the same season**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mohun Bagan Super Giant **achieved a historic milestone by winning both the **ISL League Shield** and **ISL Cup** in the 2024-25 season.
 
• This accomplishment makes them the **second team** in Indian Super League history to secure both titles in the same season.
 
• The ISL League Shield is awarded to the team finishing at the top of the league stage, while the ISL Cup is won by the team that triumphs in the playoffs.
 
• The feat reflects their **consistent performance** throughout the season, showcasing their dominance in both league and knockout phases.
 
• Mohun Bagan's achievement further solidifies their status as one of the most successful football clubs in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Super League (ISL)**

 
 
• The ISL is one of the premier football leagues in India, established in 2014 to boost football culture in the country.
 
• The league consists of two phases: the **league stage** and the **playoff stage**.
 
• The team finishing first in the league stage wins the ISL League Shield, earning qualification for the AFC Champions League.
 
• The playoffs determine the winner of the ISL Cup, which is the overall championship title.
 
 
 
• **Mohun Bagan Super Giant**
 
 
• Mohun Bagan is one of the oldest football clubs in India, founded in 1889.
 
• The club has a rich history, including winning the IFA Shield in 1911 by defeating East Yorkshire Regiment, symbolizing India's fight for independence.
 
• In 2020, the club merged with ATK to form ATK Mohun Bagan, later renamed Mohun Bagan Super Giant in 2023.
 
 
 
• **ISL League Shield and AFC Qualification**
 
 
• The League Shield winner directly qualifies for the **AFC Champions League**, which is Asia's premier club football tournament.
 
• This qualification provides Indian clubs exposure to international football and enhances the growth of Indian football.
 
 
 
• **Previous Double Winners**
 
 
• Prior to Mohun Bagan, Mumbai City FC (2020-21 season) was the first team to win both the ISL League Shield and ISL Cup in the same season.
 
• Mumbai City's achievement set a benchmark for consistency and excellence in Indian football.

questions.question: Who among the following has been appointed as the Private Secretary to the Prime Minister Narendra Modi in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nidhi Tewari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nidhi Tewari** was appointed as the Private Secretary to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in March 2025.
 
• She is a senior Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer, known for her distinguished service and expertise in administrative roles.
 
• The role of Private Secretary to the Prime Minister is critical, involving coordination, policy advisory, and administrative management at the highest level of government.
 
• Nidhi Tewari’s appointment reflects the government’s trust in experienced bureaucrats to handle sensitive and high-responsibility positions.
 
• Her appointment was approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC), which oversees high-level bureaucratic appointments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)**:

questions.question: Who among the following is appointed as the President of the upcoming COP30 Summit?

questions.question: In February 2025, the Broadcast Services Regulation Bill, 2023 was introduced in the Parliament. What is a key provision under this draft legislation?

options.text: Ban on airing foreign content between 7 p.m. and 10 p.m.

• It is expected to introduce mechanisms for **content moderation**, grievance redressal, and compliance with Indian laws across all broadcasting platforms.
 
• The bill proposes to harmonize content policies and advertising norms for cable, satellite, and OTT services, ensuring consistency and transparency for consumers and content creators.

questions.question: As per the SDG India Index 2023-24, what was the estimated percentage of reduction in the population living in multidimensional poverty between 2015-16 and 2019-21?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**From 24.8% to 14.96%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **SDG India Index 2023-24** highlights significant progress made by India in reducing multidimensional poverty.
 
• The percentage of the population living in multidimensional poverty reduced from **24.8% in 2015-16** to **14.96% in 2019-21**, showcasing a remarkable improvement.
 
• This reduction is in alignment with India’s commitment to achieving the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 1**, which focuses on ending poverty in all its forms.
 
• The achievement reflects the impact of various government initiatives, including improved healthcare, education, and living standards for economically weaker sections.
 
• The progress was measured using the **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**, which accounts for deprivations in health, education, and standard of living.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**

 
 
• The MPI is a measure developed by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** and the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)** to evaluate poverty beyond income, considering factors like health, education, and standard of living.
 
• It identifies individuals as “multidimensionally poor” if they experience deprivations in at least one-third of the weighted indicators.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• The SDGs are a set of 17 goals adopted by all United Nations Member States in 2015 to address global challenges, including poverty, inequality, climate change, and peace.
 
• **Goal 1** aims to "End poverty in all its forms everywhere."
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Reduce Poverty in India:**
 
 
• Programs like **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)**, **Ayushman Bharat**, and **National Food Security Act** have played a crucial role in improving living standards.
 
• Skill development schemes like **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)** aim to enhance employment opportunities.
 
 
 
• **India’s Progress on SDG 1:**
 
 
• India’s reduction in multidimensional poverty is a key indicator of its progress on SDG 1.
 
• Efforts have been focused on improving healthcare, education, and basic amenities to uplift marginalized communities.

questions.question: In February 2025, what was the protein isoform '1N4R tau' identified by the University of Cologne being explored for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Treating Alzheimer's disease**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **1N4R tau** is an isoform of the tau protein, which is primarily associated with neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer's disease.
 
• This isoform is characterized by having **four microtubule-binding repeat regions** and one N-terminal insertion, making it relevant for studying tauopathies.
 
• Research by the University of Cologne in February 2025 explored the role of 1N4R tau in the **pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease**, particularly its involvement in tau aggregation.
 
• 1N4R tau accumulation in brain cells leads to the formation of toxic **neurofibrillary tangles**, which are a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease.
 
• The study aimed to investigate potential therapeutic approaches to **mitigate tau-induced neurotoxicity** and slow disease progression.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tau Proteins:**

 
 
• Tau proteins are microtubule-associated proteins that stabilize microtubules in neurons.
 
• When tau proteins become hyperphosphorylated, they detach from microtubules and aggregate, leading to cell damage.
 
 
 
• **Neurofibrillary Tangles:**
 
 
• Neurofibrillary tangles are clumps of tau protein found in the brains of individuals with Alzheimer's disease.
 
• They disrupt neural communication, contributing to cognitive decline.
 
 
 
• **Alzheimer's Disease:**
 
 
• Alzheimer's is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by memory loss, cognitive impairment, and behavioral changes.
 
• It is associated with the accumulation of beta-amyloid plaques and tau tangles in the brain.
 
 
 
• **Therapeutic Exploration:**
 
 
• Current research focuses on targeting tau aggregation as a potential therapeutic approach for Alzheimer's disease.
 
• Strategies include tau inhibitors, immunotherapy, and enhancing tau clearance mechanisms.

questions.question: Which of the following forest-dwelling tribes, found in Uttarakhand, is known for seasonal migration and forest-based cattle herding?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Van Gujjar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Van Gujjars** are a nomadic forest-dwelling tribe primarily found in the state of Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, and some parts of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• They are known for their practice of seasonal migration, moving to higher altitudes during summer and returning to plains during winter, primarily for cattle grazing.
 
• The tribe depends on forest-based cattle herding for their livelihood, raising buffaloes and selling dairy products such as milk and ghee.
 
• Van Gujjars traditionally live in the forest areas, and their lifestyle is deeply intertwined with nature and forest conservation.
 
• They are advocates of sustainable forest use and often resist displacement caused by conservation projects or industrialization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nomadic Tribes:** Nomadic tribes like the Van Gujjars move seasonally to sustain their pastoral practices, which are essential for their economic survival.
 
• **Forest Rights Act, 2006:** This act recognizes the rights of forest-dwelling communities like Van Gujjars to access and use forest resources sustainably.
 
• **Challenges:** Nomadic tribes often face displacement, lack of access to healthcare and education, and conflict with forest conservation policies.
 
• **Uttarakhand's Biodiversity:** The state is rich in biodiversity, and tribes like Van Gujjars play a significant role in preserving the ecological balance through sustainable practices.
 
• **Van Gujjar Advocacy:** The tribe has been actively campaigning for the recognition of their rights, including access to grazing lands and protection against displacement.

questions.question: In April 2025, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) adjusted its monetary policy stance in response to global economic uncertainties. What was the new stance adopted by the RBI?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Accommodative**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In April 2025, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) adopted an **Accommodative monetary policy stance** to support economic growth amidst global uncertainties.
 
• An accommodative stance implies that the central bank is ready to lower interest rates or maintain low rates to inject liquidity into the economy.
 
• The decision was taken in response to **slowing global economic growth and subdued inflationary pressures**, ensuring economic stability.
 
• By adopting an accommodative stance, the RBI aimed to encourage borrowing, investment, and spending to boost economic activity in the country.
 
• This policy stance is often employed during periods of **low inflation** and sluggish economic growth to foster recovery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monetary Policy:** It refers to the measures taken by a central bank, like the RBI, to regulate the money supply and interest rates in the economy.
 
• **Accommodative Stance:** This is a policy approach where the central bank lowers interest rates or maintains them at low levels to stimulate economic growth.
 
• **Hawkish vs. Dovish Policy:** A hawkish stance focuses on controlling inflation by increasing interest rates, while a dovish or accommodative stance prioritizes economic growth by lowering rates.
 
• **Global Economic Impact:** Central banks worldwide often adjust their policies in response to global economic trends, such as changes in trade dynamics, geopolitical issues, or financial market volatility.
 
• **Inflation Targeting:** The RBI’s monetary policy framework is guided by inflation targeting, with a medium-term goal of maintaining inflation at 4% (+/- 2%). An accommodative stance is consistent with this framework during periods of low inflation.
